statement.p: Calculate the velocity and acceleration vectors, and speed for \mathbf{r}(t)=\langle \cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right),\sin\mathopen{}\left(3t\right),\cos\mathopen{}\left(3t\right) \rangle when t=\frac{5 \pi}{3}.
Usage: To enter a vector, for example \langle x,y,z\rangle, type \lt x, y, z \gt

static.solution: \mathbf{r}(t) gives velocity: \mathbf{v}(t)=\mathbf{r}'(t)=\langle -\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right), 3\cos\mathopen{}\left(3t\right), -3\sin\mathopen{}\left(3t\right)\rangle and so velocity at t=\frac{5 \pi}{3} is \mathbf{v}(5 \pi/3)=\left\langle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, -3, 0\right\rangle. Differentiating \mathbf{v}(t) gives acceleration: \mathbf{a}(t)=\mathbf{r}''(t)=\langle -\cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right), -9\sin\mathopen{}\left(3t\right), -\left(9\cos\mathopen{}\left(3t\right)\right)\rangle and so acceleration at t=\frac{5 \pi}{3} is \mathbf{a}(5 \pi/3)=\left\langle \frac{-1}{2}, 0, 9\right\rangle. The speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector: ||\mathbf{v}(5 \pi/3)||=\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2+\left(-3\right)^2+\left(0\right)^2}=3.1225.
